archetype.name: Fringe Contender (offense-first)
archetype.definition: A Dallas team whose top-five, well-protected offense keeps it in every game, but a bottom-three defense caps it at roughly average, leaving a playoff case that leans on a soft division.

report.headline: Top-five offense, last-place third-down defense: a coin-flip team with a losing record
report.take:
This is last year's Cowboys again, almost exactly. In 2025 the offense ranked 5th in EPA and the defense ranked 32nd. Through eight games of 2026 the offense is 4th (0.141 EPA a play) and the defense is 30th (0.14 allowed). Add the two together and you get a net EPA of 0.001, 18th in the league: a genuinely median team. Dak Prescott has started every game behind a line that has allowed the lowest sack rate in football. CeeDee Lamb is the clear first read with 92 targets, and George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy behind him give the passing game real depth.

The 3-5 record is a little harsher than the play. Dallas has outscored opponents by 6 points, which implies about 4 wins. It is 25% in one-score games, and two of the losses came on the final possession: 31-34 to Baltimore and 30-33 in overtime to Arizona. That is roughly one game of bad luck, though, not three. The Cowboys also lost outright as a 9.5-point favorite to Tampa Bay and as a 7-point favorite to Arizona. A defense this leaky turns comfortable spreads into coin flips.

The averages hide two splits. First, the offense has done most of its damage against middling defenses. Against the two good ones on the schedule, Tampa Bay (2nd in defensive EPA) and Green Bay (7th), Dallas scored 16 and 13 and turned it over five times. Second, the defense does not just bend, it never gets off the field. Opponents convert 52.9% of third downs, the worst rate in the league. They score touchdowns on 70.4% of red-zone trips. They lean on the run (offenses pass 5 points less than expected against Dallas) and have piled up 1,222 rushing yards. The unit has produced only 6 takeaways to stop any of it. Opposing No. 1 receivers are scoring 6.9 PPR points a game over their norm, 31st in the league.

Where it goes depends on the schedule's defenses. San Francisco, Seattle, the Rams and Jacksonville all rank top-eight on defense, the kind of opponent that has stalled this offense. Tennessee, Philadelphia twice and Washington are soft. The NFC East is weak enough that a 3-5 team sitting second behind a 4-2-1 Giants club is still in it. Expect a lot of 30-27 games, won or lost by whichever side makes the last stop.

strengths.title: Efficient passing behind elite protection
strengths.body: Dallas ranks 4th in offensive EPA and allows the league's lowest sack rate, even though Prescott holds the ball longer than most (23rd in time to throw). The line is buying him time rather than him getting it out early, which makes the protection the real asset. It also showed up last year, when the offense was 5th, so it should hold.

strengths.title: A run game that stays on schedule
strengths.body: Javonte Williams' 3.81 yards a carry looks ordinary, but the run game ranks 4th in success rate and 5th in run EPA. It keeps Dallas ahead of the chains rather than breaking big plays. When the passing threat is respected, it can take over, as it did with 204 yards at Philadelphia.

strengths.title: Aggressive on fourth down
strengths.body: Schottenheimer has gone for it on every fourth-down chance the model flags as a go, the most aggressive rate in the league. With a defense this porous, playing for points rather than field position is the right call. It helps keep the scoring pace that the defense requires.

concerns.title: A defense that can't get off the field
concerns.body: Dallas ranks last in third-down defense and 26th in red-zone touchdown rate, so drives that should end in punts or field goals end in sevens. This is not a slow start. The defense was also 32nd in EPA allowed in 2025, so it is a two-year structural problem rather than noise likely to correct.

concerns.title: No takeaways, little pressure
concerns.body: The defense has only 6 takeaways and ranks 28th in QB hit rate, so it neither wins on third-and-long nor steals possessions. The 5-sack game against Arizona was the outlier. A unit without disruption has no way to cover for the coverage leaks against top receivers.

concerns.title: Offense stalls against good defenses
concerns.body: Against Tampa Bay and Green Bay, the two top-ten defenses Dallas has faced, the passing game went negative and gave the ball away five times across the pair. The rest of the schedule has four top-eight defenses. The offense's ranking may be partly a product of the opponents it has seen.

trend.note: Dallas has alternated shootout wins with losses all year. A two-game offensive slump against Tampa Bay and Green Bay gave way to a 38-point game at Philadelphia, then an overtime loss to Arizona. The defense has been consistently poor throughout; the offense's level against the opponent decides each week.

nextGame.headline: Clean pockets for Prescott, but the Colts' run game is the test
nextGame.body:
Dallas goes to Indianapolis as a 6-point favorite against a 2-6 team whose offense ranks 27th in EPA and 31st passing. On paper that is the best matchup the Dallas defense has seen in weeks. The catch is that the Colts do one thing well: run the ball, with the 5th-best rushing EPA, and they rank 5th in time of possession. That points straight at the Cowboys' run funnel. On the other side, Indy's pass rush ranks 29th in pressure rate, so Prescott should have time. The Colts defend No. 1 and No. 2 receivers well, though, and are 4th on third downs. Dallas has already lost twice this year as a bigger favorite than this.

Availability tilts toward the Dallas offense and away from its defense. Both safeties, Caleb Downs (93% of snaps) and P.J. Locke, are in the concussion protocol, LB Dee Winters is out and LB Malachi Lawrence is questionable. That thins the second level of a defense that already leaks against the run. TE Jake Ferguson is questionable with TE Luke Schoonmaker out, which matters because tight ends have been productive against Indianapolis. The Colts are without CB Justin Walley, a 72%-snap starter, and have CB Cam Taylor-Britt on injured reserve, so their secondary depth is tested too.

waysToWin.title: Work the slot, tight end and backs
waysToWin.body: Indianapolis is stingy against opposing WR1s and WR2s but ranks 31st in EPA allowed to WR3s, and lead backs and tight ends have outscored their norms against it. With Walley out, Flournoy, Williams out of the backfield and Ferguson, if he plays, are the soft spots to target ahead of forcing it to Lamb.

waysToWin.title: Clean pocket against a weak rush
waysToWin.body: The league's best sack-rate protection faces a pass rush that ranks 29th in pressure rate. If Prescott sits untouched, Dallas should hit the high-20s in points it usually needs. That is more than a 22-point Colts offense typically matches.

waysToWin.title: Get ahead and make Jones throw
waysToWin.body: Daniel Jones runs the 31st-ranked passing offense behind a line with a 22nd-ranked sack rate, and Indy's turnover margin is the worst in the league. An early lead takes the Colts' run game away and forces them into the dropbacks where this Dallas defense can finally create a takeaway.

waysToLose.title: Colts grind it out on the ground
waysToLose.body: Offenses already run more than expected against Dallas, and Indianapolis has a top-five rushing EPA and a top-five time of possession. With Winters out and both starting safeties in the protocol, long drives could keep Prescott on the sideline and shrink the game. A shorter game makes the 6-point favorite vulnerable.

waysToLose.title: Losing the third-down battle
waysToLose.body: Dallas allows the highest third-down conversion rate in the league, and the Colts' defense is 4th on third downs. If Indy extends drives and Dallas' offense stalls in obvious passing downs, the efficiency edge disappears.

waysToLose.title: Forcing it to Lamb
waysToLose.body: Indianapolis ranks 4th in EPA allowed to WR1s. Dallas' worst games came when the passing game turned it over, as in the three-giveaway loss to Tampa Bay. Gifting a turnover-starved Colts team short fields is how Dallas loses to a 2-6 opponent.

nextGame.watch: Watch the Colts' early-down runs against a Dallas front missing Winters. If Indy is in second-and-short all day, this becomes another one-score game.

restOfSeason.body:
The offense is real and should keep scoring in the high-20s against average or worse defenses: Tennessee, Philadelphia, Washington and this week's Colts. The tougher tests are San Francisco, Seattle, the Rams and Jacksonville, and its scoring will likely dip against those top-eight defenses, as it did against Tampa Bay and Green Bay. The defense has two years of evidence behind its struggles and a thinning injury list, so do not bank on it improving. What should even out is the close-game record. A 25% one-score win rate for a team with a positive point differential tends to drift back toward the middle, and that is worth perhaps a win.

That adds up to roughly a .500 finish. In this NFC East, where the leader is 4-2-1, that keeps Dallas in the division race into December. The three closing division games and the home date with Philadelphia are the swing stretch.
swingFactors: Offense against the four top-eight defenses left
Health of Downs and the linebacker group

confidence.note: Eight games, but the profile closely matches 2025's, which makes it more credible.
